"""Starting architecture: the main campaign's default policy (conv encoder, width 64, depth 2, ReLU,
no normalisation), rewritten as a candidate file. A 3x3 conv body, a 1x1 conv placement head
(one logit per brick type and anchor cell), and DONE and value heads on mean+max pooled features."""
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

WIDTH = 64
DEPTH = 2


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels
        for _ in range(DEPTH):
            layers += [nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU()]
            c_in = WIDTH
        self.body = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        place = self.place_head(f).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: No trials have run yet. The starting recipe's four seeds scored 0.068 three times and 0.258 once. That suggests training runs either break through or stall, depending on the seed. The default recipe also makes very few policy updates: 256 envs × 16 steps = 4,096 samples per update, which gives only about 32 updates in 131k steps. A recipe that makes more, smaller updates, or that uses fewer epochs so the budget pays for more samples, should make the breakthrough more likely. The budget rule rewards fewer epochs: 2 epochs give about 243k steps and 1 epoch gives about 426k. This round tests three points in that space, changing roughly one thing each, so I can tell which matters: update count, sample count, or both. Since one seed in four already reaches 0.258, a two-seed mean differs by chance by about 0.1, so only clear gains will count.
analyses.2: All three round-1 recipes scored exactly 0.0684 on both seeds. That is 35 of 512 designs. The baseline also hit this score on 3 of its 4 seeds. So 0.0684 looks like a fixed local optimum, probably a simple greedy fill policy that only solves easy designs. It is not seed noise. Changing the number of updates, the number of epochs or the number of samples (from 131k up to 426k) did not move it. The lone 0.258 seed shows that escaping is possible. The bottleneck therefore seems to be escaping this plateau, not sample efficiency. Three levers could address that. First, more exploration (entropy) to stop the policy collapsing early. Second, more credit for the +1 exact-build bonus at episode end (gamma and lambda), so finishing exactly matters more than partial fill. Third, gentler updates (lower lr) so the policy does not lock in the greedy habit early. I test each lever on its own, using the default batch layout otherwise.
analyses.3: Outcomes are bimodal. Most runs settle on a 0.068 plateau, probably a simple greedy strategy that only solves trivial designs. Some seeds break out to between 0.26 and 0.33 (baseline seed 3, and seed 2 of r2c1). Changing how many updates or samples we get (r1c1 to r1c3), lengthening the horizon (r2c2) or lowering lr (r2c3) did not break the plateau, and lower lr did slightly worse. Only raising entropy to 0.03 gave a breakout, which hints that exploration is the lever. With 2 seeds per trial, a single breakout is weak evidence (the baseline broke out on 1 of 4 seeds too). This round therefore tests more entropy (0.05). It also pairs ent 0.03 with more samples (2 epochs gives about 243k steps) to allow more time to break out, and with a higher lr to see whether faster policy movement helps escape the plateau.
analyses.4: Recipe changes at the default entropy of 0.01 all stayed on the 0.068 plateau: more updates, fewer epochs, a longer horizon and a lower lr. Raising entropy is what got runs off the plateau. Entropy 0.03 scored 0.20, 0.05 scored 0.22, and both had one seed at 0.068 or a wide gap between seeds. Entropy 0.03 with lr 2e-3 reached 0.375, and both seeds were well clear of the plateau (0.33 and 0.42). That suggests a faster learning rate plus exploration is what drives breakouts. Lowering lr hurt and spending the budget on more samples with fewer epochs did not help, so the budget is best spent on 4 epochs and strong updates. In this last round, two candidates push further along the winning direction (higher lr, and higher entropy at lr 2e-3). The third keeps the best recipe but updates the policy twice as often with the same number of gradient steps, which only showed up as a failure at low entropy.
